    Push-down constructions and Theorem 5.2 #

    Alternatives (2) and (3) of Theorem 3.14 share one shape: a fully faithful exact functor L : D → Rep D into representations of a finite quiver D, followed by the push-down along a quiver morphism p : D → Q into modules over A, presented as a quotient π : kQ → A (Constructions 3.6, 3.7 and 3.12). A PdData k A records these data together with the hypotheses of PushDown.bl_self_eq_zero (a partition of block positions into classes, and the vanishing of morphisms whose image vanishes at a vertex), the condition that the kernel of π acts by zero on p_*L(T), and the facts behind the colimit comparison: every vector of L(T) comes from L(U) for a finite-dimensional U ⊆ T, and L keeps inclusions injective.

    The functor F = p_*L : D → Mod A is additive, k-linear, faithful and exact, has finite-dimensional values on D_fin, satisfies the colimit comparison (3.6), and admits retractions on C with a nilpotence bound, the number of vertices of D (Propositions 4.4, 4.7, 4.8). With the two facts about S₋ (PdDatum) it gives the data of Theorem 5.2. A kernel of π acting by zero on p_*L(T) for finite-dimensional T acts by zero for every T (kills_of_fin, as in the proof of Lemma 3.13).

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.PushDown.kills_of_fin {k : Type u} [Field k] {D Q : FinQuiver} (L : CategoryTheory.Functor (Statement.D k) (Rep k D)) (finitary : ∀ (T : Statement.D k) (i : D.V) (x : ↑((L.obj T).obj i)), ∃ (U : Kron.FinSub T.obj), x ∈ Set.range ⇑(ModuleCat.Hom.hom ((L.map (Comparison.incl T U)).app i))) (p : D.Hom Q) (z : FinQuiver.PathAlgebra k Q) (h : ∀ (T : Dfin k), (Rep.pdAct p (L.obj ((DfinToD k).obj T))) z = 0) (T : Statement.D k) :
    (Rep.pdAct p (L.obj T)) z = 0

    structure LargeIndecomposable.PushDown.PdData (k : Type u) [Field k] (A : Type u) [Ring A] [Algebra k A] :
    Type (u + 1)

    The data of a push-down construction, apart from the representation-embedding property.

    • D : FinQuiver

      The quiver carrying the representations L(T).

    • Q : FinQuiver

      The quiver of the presentation of A.

    • p : self.D.Hom self.Q

      The quiver morphism along which we push down.

    • locInj : self.p.LocallyInjective
    • B : BlockClasses self.p

      The classes of block positions.

    • L : CategoryTheory.Functor (Statement.D k) (Rep k self.D)

      The functor L.

    • additive : self.L.Additive
    • hL : self.L.FullyFaithful
    • map_smul {T U : Statement.D k} (c : k) (f : T ⟶ U) (i : self.D.V) : (self.L.map (c • f)).app i = c • (self.L.map f).app i
    • zero : ZeroAtVertex self.L
    • exact (X Y Z : Statement.D k) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : Statement.Kron.IsShortExact f.hom g.hom → ∀ (i : self.D.V), Function.Injective ⇑(ModuleCat.Hom.hom ((self.L.map f).app i)) ∧ Function.Surjective ⇑(ModuleCat.Hom.hom ((self.L.map g).app i)) ∧ (ModuleCat.Hom.hom ((self.L.map f).app i)).range = (ModuleCat.Hom.hom ((self.L.map g).app i)).ker
    • fin (T : Dfin k) (i : self.D.V) : Module.Finite k ↑((self.L.obj ((DfinToD k).obj T)).obj i)
    • finitary (T : Statement.D k) (i : self.D.V) (x : ↑((self.L.obj T).obj i)) : ∃ (U : Kron.FinSub T.obj), x ∈ Set.range ⇑(ModuleCat.Hom.hom ((self.L.map (Comparison.incl T U)).app i))

      Every vector of L(T) comes from L(U) for a finite-dimensional U ⊆ T.

    • incl_injective (T : Statement.D k) (U : Kron.FinSub T.obj) (i : self.D.V) : Function.Injective ⇑(ModuleCat.Hom.hom ((self.L.map (Comparison.incl T U)).app i))

      L keeps the inclusions U ⊆ T injective.

    • π : FinQuiver.PathAlgebra k self.Q →ₐ[k] A

      The presentation kQ → A.

    • surj : Function.Surjective ⇑self.π

                        Statement.IsIndecomposable A ↑(W.functor.obj S)
